newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds up on issue cancellation.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds up on issue cancellation.

text.p: 1620 GMT - Austrian bonds closed firmer but off earlier highs on Thursday, driven by a strong performance by the German Bund future and the cancellation of a recent bond issue in Austria, traders said.
The Austrian Kontrollbank (OKB), which handles the government's bond issues, said today Austria's federal financing agency was set to cancel a bond auction originally planned for Dec 3.
Sources at the agency said the issue had been cancelled because there was no need for further bond issues this year. The move had the effect of shifting focus to the spot market.
"The spot market outperformed the futures market," said one trader.
* Latest 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 up 15 bps at 100.20 to yield 5.84 (5.86) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.22/100.32 to yield 5.84/83.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 steady at 102.95 to yield 4.76 (4.76) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 103.15/25 to yield 4.71/69 percent.
* 10-year spread to German bunds down one at nine bps, five-year spread down three at 17 bps.
* December AGB future up 30 bps at 107.65 on volume of 479 contracts.
* Money market rates mixed with three-month VIBOR steady at 3.350 and overnight money down at 3.05/30. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
